questions.question: Which member of the structured-prompt quartet does the lesson call the highest-leverage one?
questions.explanation: See the "The quartet: role, task, constraints, format" section: the output format is "the highest-leverage member of the quartet".

questions.question: In the demo, the v1 loose-paragraph prompt yielded prose with only 2 of 4 fields reliably parsed. What was the root cause?
options: The model lacked domain knowledge about the email
The prompt did not assign a role
No output format was declared, so conversational inertia produced prose
The sampling parameters such as temperature were not lowered
questions.explanation: See the "The format declaration pins the prose instinct" section: the model's default inertia is conversation, and the v1 output lost 2 of 4 fields because the format was never declared.

questions.question: According to the lesson, what is the typical symptom of over-constraining?
options: Output falls back to prose that cannot be parsed
The model refuses the task outright
The prompt's input token cost rises sharply
The model squeezes to fit, inventing field content to fill the frame
questions.explanation: See the "The price of over-constraining" section: pinned too hard, the model starts squeezing to fit — the fields are filled, but the values are invented.
